title: Connecticut POST General Notice 25-05 — Further waiver of citizenship requirement
summary: Official March 21, 2025 POST notice documenting the 2020 permanent-legal-resident waiver and the March 13, 2025 extension to DACA recipients.

evidence.claim: POST General Notice 25-05 states that regulation 7-294e-16(c) contains the citizenship requirement, that POSTC partially waived it on November 19, 2020 for permanent legal residents, and that POSTC further waived it on March 13, 2025 for DACA recipients.

caveats: The notice establishes POSTC's waiver policy and dates; it does not establish any individual applicant's citizenship or immigration status.

title: Danbury police eligibility amendment — POSTC waiver authority and September publication state
summary: Primary state records resolve the previously open POSTC citizenship-waiver lineage: the regulatory baseline remains citizenship, but POSTC waived it for permanent legal residents in 2020 and DACA recipients in 2025, and the current POSTC-51 form reflects all three eligible categories. Danbury's September 1 final minutes remain unpublished in the official Agenda Center as of this pass.

evidence.claim: The official Connecticut eRegulations page retains Sec. 7-294e-16(c)'s baseline US-citizenship requirement; POST General Notice 25-05 explicitly identifies the later waivers and the current POSTC-51 form reflects them.

As observed September 15, 2026, the official Danbury City Council Agenda Center lists the September 1, 2026 meeting and agenda but no minutes for that meeting; the City Council page states that minutes are available following approval.

caveats: This pass reconciles policy authority and publication state only; it does not infer or record any individual's citizenship, immigration status, ethnicity, or national origin.
A blank minutes field is publication-state evidence only, not proof that the meeting did not occur, the ordinance failed, or approved minutes do not exist elsewhere.

findings: Connecticut regulation 7-294e-16(c) preserves a baseline US-citizenship requirement for probationary police candidates.
POST General Notice 25-05 says POSTC extended eligibility to permanent legal residents on November 19, 2020 and to DACA recipients on March 13, 2025 under its waiver authority.
POSTC-51 Rev. 3/25 operationalizes the waiver by listing US citizen, Permanent Legal Resident, or DACA recipient as the appointment eligibility line.
Danbury's citizen/LPR/DACA applicant categories therefore align with the current POSTC eligibility categories identified in the state primary records.
As of September 15, 2026, Danbury's official City Council Agenda Center still exposes the September 1 agenda but no posted minutes for that meeting.
conclusions: The prior canonical policy gap about the underlying POSTC 2020 and 2025 waiver record is resolved by primary state records.
The state-level waiver does not identify or imply the citizenship or immigration status of any individual Danbury officer or applicant.
Final Danbury enactment details remain unresolved until the approved September 1 minutes, enacted/codified text, or another authoritative final legislative record is published or recovered.
counterarguments: The regulatory text alone still says citizen; reading it without the later POSTC waiver notice and current POSTC-51 form would misstate the operational appointment standard.
No posted minutes in the Agenda Center is not evidence that the ordinance failed, was not voted on, or lacks legal effect.
unresolved: Approved September 1, 2026 City Council minutes and roll-call disposition, including primary-source attribution of both NO votes.

title: Research pass: Danbury PD POSTC citizenship-waiver reconciliation (2026-09-15)
summary: Worker 2 bounded continuation resolving the authoritative POSTC waiver lineage and recording the current September 1 minutes-publication state without inferring any officer's immigration or citizenship status.

data.research_question: What authoritative Connecticut POSTC records govern the citizenship-status eligibility categories underlying Danbury's 2026 police-applicant amendment, and what final September 1 primary municipal record is publicly available now?
data.method: Searched the existing Danbury corpus and issue history first, then reviewed Connecticut POST General Notice 25-05, current POSTC-51 Rev. 3/25, the official Connecticut eRegulations entry-level rule, and the live Danbury City Council Agenda Center. Separated the regulatory baseline from later waivers and treated missing posted minutes only as a bounded publication-state observation.
classification_rules: Treat regulation 7-294e-16(c) as the baseline rule and POSTC's later waiver notice/form as the operative expansion of eligible appointment categories.
Never infer citizenship, immigration status, ethnicity, or national origin for any individual officer or applicant.
A blank minutes field in the municipal index is publication-state evidence only, not proof of legislative outcome.

findings.finding: POSTC primary records establish the 2020 permanent-legal-resident waiver and March 2025 DACA extension and show both reflected in POSTC-51 Rev. 3/25.
Danbury's official Agenda Center still had no posted September 1 minutes at the time of this pass, so final roll-call/enactment claims remain open.
